# Block 4: Context, disclosure and autonomy {.unnumbered}

```{r}
#| include: false
source("R/booktem_setup.R")

library(tidyverse)

```

:::{.callout-note}
**Last verified:** 9 October 2026, against GitHub's Copilot documentation
(plans, IDE agent and plan modes), the Claude Code documentation (permission
modes) and the Posit Assistant documentation (docs version 1.7).
:::

Two questions decide how far you can trust anything an AI assistant does with
your code:

1. **What can it see?** Its answers are only as good as its context, and
   everything it sees has left your machine.
2. **What can it do?** An assistant that advises leaves you as the filter on
   every change. An agent that acts removes that filter.

This block covers both, using the three tools in this course: Claude Code in the
terminal, Posit Assistant in RStudio or Positron, and GitHub Copilot, both in
the browser and as an asynchronous cloud agent.

*⏱ ~55 minutes*


# Part A: What can the assistant see? {.unnumbered}

| Surface | Example | What it can see | Can it act? |
|---|---|---|---|
| Browser chat | Copilot Chat on github.com; any chat website | What you paste; on github.com, files in the repository you open it from | No |
| Session-aware IDE assistant | Posit Assistant in RStudio or Positron | Your live R session (loaded packages, data frames, console history) and project files | Yes, in your session and files |
| Terminal agent | Claude Code | Project files, and the output of any command it runs | Yes, in your files and shell |
| Remote agent | Copilot cloud agent | The repository on GitHub, in an environment GitHub runs | Yes, on a branch; returns a pull request |

:::{.callout-note}
**Knowing versus guessing.** An assistant can describe your data confidently
for two quite different reasons: it has been given real information, or it is
recalling patterns from training data. Only the first is reliable.

It has real information when you pasted the output, when it read a file, when
the IDE injected your session, or when it ran code and read the result. It is
guessing when none of those apply. The tells are a well-known dataset you never
mentioned (`mtcars`, `iris`, `penguins`) or column names and values you never
supplied.

Even with context, a model's account of *what it can see* is unreliable. Check
any data-specific claim against the real object.
:::


## Exercise 1: Context decides the answer

:::{.task}
::::{.task-header}
The same error, three levels of context (15 minutes)
::::
::::{.task-container}

**1. Error only.** In a browser chat, open a fresh session and paste only this,
asking "What does this error mean?":

```
Error in `mutate()`:
ℹ In argument: `mass_change = mass_post - mass_pre_g`.
Caused by error:
! object 'mass_post' not found
```

The answer can only reason from the error text.

**2. Error plus code plus structure.** In a new session, paste:

```
I am running this code:

  voles |>
    mutate(mass_change = mass_post - mass_pre_g)

and getting:

  Error in `mutate()`:
  ℹ In argument: `mass_change = mass_post - mass_pre_g`.
  Caused by error:
  ! object 'mass_post' not found

The data structure is:

  Rows: 72
  Columns: 6
  $ subject_id          <chr> "V001", "V002", "V003", ...
  $ sex                 <chr> "M", "F", "M", ...
  $ treatment_arm       <chr> "Control", "Control", ...
  $ mass_pre_g          <dbl> 28.3, 27.9, 30.1, ...
  $ mass_post_g         <dbl> 28.5, 28.0, 30.5, ...
  $ metabolic_rate_post <dbl> 13.21, 12.84, 13.55, ...

What is wrong?
```

It should name the missing `_g` suffix.

**3. No paste at all.** Load the data in your R session, run the failing code,
then ask Posit Assistant (or Claude Code, from the project folder) only: "Why
did my last command fail?" A session-aware assistant can read your console
history and the data frame; Claude Code can open the script and run code to
inspect the data.

Then ask: "How do you know the column names?" Compare its answer with what you
know it was given. If it claims to have seen something it could not have seen,
you have found the unreliability described in the callout above.

::::
:::

The lesson is not that one route is correct. The answer is only as good as the
context, and context reaches the model by more than one route.


## Disclosure: every route out of your machine

Everything an assistant sees is sent to a model provider. Data leave your
machine by four routes:

1. **What you paste.** Errors, outputs, printed results.
2. **Files it reads.** A data file in the repository or project folder.
3. **Session context the IDE injects.** Posit Assistant reads loaded packages,
   data frames and console history, so a data frame in memory can reach the
   model without any paste.
4. **Output of commands it runs.** If an agent runs `print(voles)` or
   `head data.csv`, those values enter its context.

Before you decide what to show, know what the surface can already reach. A data
file committed to the repository, or a tibble loaded in your session, may
already be disclosed.

When you describe a data frame deliberately, three commands reveal increasing
amounts:

- `names(voles)` lists column names only, in their original order.
- `summary(voles)` adds ranges, quartiles and missing-value counts for numeric
  columns: the shape of the data, not individual records.
- `glimpse(voles)` or `str(voles)` adds the first few actual values of every
  column.

:::{.callout-important}
**Before using an assistant on research data**, check three things: whether
your institution permits sending this kind of data to this provider; whether
your ethics approval and data-sharing agreements allow it; and whether a
synthetic or anonymised copy would serve instead. Tool settings that restrict
reading (see the [enforced-controls block](11f-enforced-controls.qmd)) reduce accidental exposure, but they
do not make an agent safe for confidential data: any command it runs that
prints data sends that data to the provider.
:::


## Exercise 2: Context you hold in your head

:::{.task}
::::{.task-header}
Refine an approach question (10 minutes)
::::
::::{.task-container}

**1.** In a fresh browser chat, ask exactly:

```
I have a dataset with pre and post measurements. How should I analyse it?
```

With no design and no question supplied, you will get a tour of options
(paired tests, change scores, ANCOVA, mixed models) rather than a
recommendation.

**2.** In a new session, state the design and the question:

```
I have 72 voles, balanced across three treatment arms (Control, Low_dose,
High_dose) and two sexes (M, F). Each animal has body mass measured before
and after treatment, and a single post-treatment metabolic-rate reading.

My question is whether the high-dose treatment changes mass relative to
control, and whether the effect differs between sexes.

The dataset is small (n = 12 per cell). I will report effect sizes alongside
any inferential test. Given this design, what is a defensible primary
analysis, and what are the main threats to its validity?
```

**3.** Compare the answers. A data file can supply column names and types, but
not your scientific question or your design intent. Those exist only in your
head until you write them down.

Treat even the better answer as a proposal to check against a statistics text
or a colleague. Choosing the primary analysis is your decision, not the
assistant's.

::::
:::


# Part B: What can the assistant do? {.unnumbered}

The model is the same at every level below. What changes is what it is
permitted to do, and therefore where you sit in the loop.

| Rung | What happens | Claude Code | Posit Assistant | GitHub Copilot |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0. Suggest | Completes the line you are typing | — | Next Edit Suggestions | Inline suggestions |
| 1. Ask | Answers; changes nothing | Ask a question in `plan` mode | Ask mode | Ask in Chat |
| 2. Plan | Proposes steps; changes nothing until you approve | `plan` mode | `/plan` | Plan mode in the IDE |
| 3. Act, with approval | Edits files and runs commands, asking first | `default` mode | Normal mode | Agent mode, approving each tool call |
| 4. Act, partly unsupervised | Some actions without asking | `acceptEdits` mode | Auto mode | Agent mode with auto-approval |
| 5. Act, unsupervised | No prompts | `bypassPermissions` | YOLO mode | — |
| 6. Act remotely | Works on a branch elsewhere; returns a pull request | — | — | Cloud agent |

In Claude Code, `Shift+Tab` cycles `default`, `acceptEdits` and `plan`. In Posit
Assistant, `/plan`, `/auto`, `/yolo` and `/restricted` switch modes. Use rungs 0
to 3 throughout this course. Do not use rung 5.

:::{.callout-warning}
**Read the rung's small print.** `acceptEdits` in Claude Code approves more than
edits: it also auto-approves common file commands such as `mkdir`, `touch`, `mv`
and `cp`. A `cp` that overwrites a raw data file needs no approval in that mode.
Posit Assistant's auto mode replaces your judgement with a classifier model's.
Each step up the ladder removes a moment when you would have seen the action
before it happened.

**Approval fatigue is real.** At rung 3, an approval prompt you click through
without reading is rung 5 with extra steps. The [enforced-controls block](11f-enforced-controls.qmd) covers
the rules that hold however tired you are.
:::

Higher rungs make standing instructions matter more. In Ask mode, a convention
the assistant does not know costs you a re-read. In agent mode, the assistant
acts on its guess, and the guess lands in your files. That is why the
[instructions-and-skills block](11e-instructions-skills.qmd) comes next, and why the [enforced-controls block](11f-enforced-controls.qmd)
follows it.


## Exercise 3: The same task, rising autonomy

:::{.task}
::::{.task-header}
Ask, plan, act (20 minutes)
::::
::::{.task-container}

Use your forked workshop repository, **committed and clean**, so every change is
a diff you can inspect or revert. Never run an agent with uncommitted work you
are not prepared to lose.

**1. Ask.** At rung 1, ask:

```
In scripts/clean_voles.R, how would I add a column mass_change equal to
mass_post_g minus mass_pre_g?
```

Read the answer. Confirm with `git status` that nothing changed.

**2. Plan.** At rung 2, give a goal that spans several files:

```
In the voles pipeline, add a derived mass_change column (mass_post_g minus
mass_pre_g) in the cleaning step, create a new script that plots mass_change
by treatment_arm, and make sure the pipeline still runs end to end.
```

Before approving, check that the plan names every file it will touch, does not
touch raw data, says where the plot script goes, and says how it will check the
pipeline runs. Amend the plan in conversation if any of that is missing.

**3. Act, with approval.** Approve the plan and stay at rung 3. Read each
approval prompt before answering it. Refuse at least one action you consider
out of scope, and note how the agent responds.

**4. Review.** When it finishes:

```bash
git status
git diff
```

Read the diff as you would a colleague's contribution. The agent's statement
that the pipeline "still runs" is a claim; run the pipeline yourself to check
it.

**5. Compare.** At which rung did you decide the most? At which rung would you
have missed an unwanted change if you had not read the diff?

The asynchronous rung, the Copilot cloud agent, is demonstrated in the
[characterisation-test block](11i-characterisation-tests.qmd), where its pull request meets a review gate.

::::
:::


:::{.callout-note}
**Access and cost.** Plans and prices change; check before the session.

- **Claude Code** needs an Anthropic account, used through a subscription or an
  API key; see Anthropic's documentation for current options.
- **Posit Assistant** uses Posit AI Pass or your own provider key, including an
  Anthropic API key. In RStudio, providers are configured in the assistant's
  settings.
- **GitHub Copilot** bills in AI credits. Copilot Free includes only limited
  agent features. Check GitHub's plans page to see whether your plan includes
  the cloud agent.
- **Your institution** may have approved some of these tools and not others.
:::


## Check your understanding

**What can a session-aware assistant such as Posit Assistant see that a browser
chat cannot?**

`r longmcq(c(
  "Nothing; both see only what you paste",
  answer = "Your live R session, including loaded packages, data frames in memory and console history, without your pasting anything",
  "Every file on your computer",
  "The data of other users of the same tool"
))`

**In Claude Code's acceptEdits mode, what does the agent do without asking?**

`r longmcq(c(
  "Nothing; acceptEdits only changes how diffs are displayed",
  "Only edits to files you have named",
  answer = "It edits files and runs common file commands such as cp and mv without asking, but still asks before other shell commands",
  "Everything, including all shell commands"
))`

**Which check still works whatever rung the agent ran at?**

`r longmcq(c(
  "The agent's own report that the task succeeded",
  "The approval prompts you saw during the session",
  answer = "Inspecting the changes with git status and git diff, and running the code yourself",
  "The plan the agent proposed before starting"
))`
